messages:
Lina C: Heads-up — ACME Ops flagged recurring latency spikes during peak hours. They're midmarket, heavy chat usage, renewal in 45 days. Can we draft a concise customer-facing checklist (handout) they can follow to stabilize latency + retention? Need steps for quick wins (no infra changes) and longer-term (dedicated capacity suggestions).

Alex G: +1. I'll outline practical controls: client batching, short-prefix caching, stream fallbacks, and a small warmup script they can run. Keep it a 1-page ops checklist.

Maria P: Add a short troubleshooting flow for "spike during rollout" (how to check model routing and fallback). Customers often miss the simple route mismatch.

Kevin R: For onboarding: include a single curl snippet to exercise the warm cache and a config example for client-side batching. Real teams copy/paste those.

Lina C: Can someone draft the handout text here? I'll convert to PDF and send to ACME. Aim for actionable bullets and exact commands.

Alex G: Draft below — feel free to edit. It's customer-facing but technical.

Alex G: === BEGIN CHECKLIST ===
1) Quick smoke (5 min)
- Run this warmup to populate prefix KVs and reduce first-token latency:

  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"<your top 20 prompts>"}'

- Expected: 95th pct downstream latency drops by ~200–400ms within a few requests.

2) Client-side micro-batching (low effort)
- Bundle 3–5 concurrent short requests into a single call to reduce per-token overhead. Example pseudo: 

  requests = [r1, r2, r3]
  sdk.generate(batch=requests, batch_mode="concat")

- Start with batch_size=3, verify quality. Watch for cost vs latency tradeoff.

3) Short-prefix caching (no infra change)
- Cache the first ~32 tokens of frequent prompts on your edge (TTL 10–60s). If using our SDK, enable `enable_prefix_cache: true`.

4) Stream-safe fallback (immediate mitigation)
- If streaming stalls, fall back to non-streamed generate with model variant `redwood-alpha-1-lite` (lower mem, slightly higher lat variance).

5) Monitoring checklist (what we need from you)
- 1-hour p95 before/after warmup
- Example traces (attach a single 10-request export)
- Any A/B rollout times and traffic percentages for the past 24h

6) When to request Dedicated capacity
- If sustained p95 > 1s during business hours or burst concurrency > 300 req/sec, request a capacity review. We'll propose a 2-week pilot.

7) Quick troubleshooting flow (3 steps)
- Confirm routing: `GET /v1/status` -> check `model_variant` matches expected.
- Check cache headers: look for `x-rd-cache: hit|miss`.
- If failures spike after deploy, pause rollout and switch to `redwood-alpha-1-stable`.

=== END CHECKLIST ===

Jamie M: This is great. Add one short note about "capture user impact" so CS can quantify renewal risk: include an example metric line to show execs.

Alex G: Good call. I'll append a short "impact snapshot" sample.

Alex G: Impact snapshot (copyable)

- Baseline p95 (last 7d): 820ms
- Peak p95 (today): 1.45s
- Avg tokens per request: 78
- Estimated extra cost/day from retries: $420
- Suggested action: run warmup + enable micro-batching; expected p95 reduction 200–400ms

Maria P: Also add where to upload logs for us: `https://uploads.redwood.ai/cs/` and the preferred filename pattern: `acme-<env>-traces-<YYYYMMDD>.zip`

Kevin R: Tiny UX tip for the handout: put the warmup curl and the SDK batch snippet side-by-side, with a 1-line explanation for each. That helps engineers copy/paste.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: warmup-helper v2 scheduled for release to hosted docs at 2026-03-22T18:00Z.

Lina C: Perfect — I'll finalize and share with ACME this afternoon. Thanks everyone. I'll attach the PDF and ask them to run warmup + send traces. :white_check_mark: 

Jamie M: If they run and we still see spikes, let's schedule a 30-min deep dive and offer a dedicated-capacity pilot. I'll own that follow-up. :calendar:

Alex G: I'll also prepare a short demo screencast (2–3 min) showing the warmup and batch toggle in the SDK. Link to follow. :movie_camera:

Lina C: Closing the thread — final PDF will be uploaded to the account folder and I'll post the link in the ticket.
